key_insight: CFD-driven symbolic regression learns interpretable corrections to a RANS transition model, retaining 11 of 21 candidate terms with comparable or slightly better accuracy than grid-search tuning.
engineering_relevance: Better transition predictions can improve estimates of skin friction, heat transfer and losses in turbomachinery.
method: Correct intermittency production and destruction activation functions in the local k–ω–γ model using pressure-gradient polynomials and bounded exponential feature functions.
Fit coefficients against LES mean-velocity data with gradient-free, solver-in-the-loop optimization accelerated by POD–Kriging field surrogates.
Select elastic-net hyperparameters through bi-level optimization with leave-one-case-out cross-validation.
evidence_signal: Trained on ERCOFTAC T3 flat-plate LES data, the model transferred without retraining to the transonic LS89 cascade, improving heat-transfer predictions at all four operating points and reducing errors by up to 70%.
watch_item: Residual transition-onset and transition-length errors indicate that flat-plate-only training limits predictive coverage.
paper_title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
